sentences.text:
Petitioners, accused in FIR No.I-17/2012 registered with Gholvad Police Station,
District Thane for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 465, 466, 467, 471 read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code, P.H. Jayani 214 WP1499.2013.doc have preferred this Petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India for quashing of the said F.I.R.
2) Heard Mr. Gangal, learned Advocate for the Petitioners and Mr. S.V. Gavand,
learned APP for the State.
Perused the record.
3) Record indicates that, by Order dated 29 th April, 2013 notice was issued to the Respondent no.2.
Thereafter, Respondent No.2 noted his appearance through his counsel Mr. Dinesh Patankar.

By Order dated 08 th May, 2013 it was directed that,
the Investigating Officer may continue with the investigation but shall not submit the final report without the leave of the Court.

4) The impugned F.I.R. is registered on the report of Respondent No.2 wherein it is narrated that, at the relevant time, when Respondent No.2 was visiting concerned Talathi and Tahsil office to get his ancestral landed property along with a bungalow mutated in his and brothers' name, he met with accused Subodh Parab.

On inquiry,
Respondent No.2 disclosed to Subodh Parab his object of visiting said offices.
Subodh Parab assured that, he would get the mutation done with the help of his acquaintance Mr. Deepak Mankar and Mr. Machchhi, Advocate.
Since Subodh Parab was known to Respondent No.2, he trusted him.

In April 2011, as suggested by Mr. Mankar, Mr.
Machchhi Advocate and Subodh Parab, Respondent No.2 gave his and his brothers'
photos to Mr. Machchhi for the purpose of mutation and the later also took his signatures on 3 to 4 blank papers and P.H. Jayani 214 WP1499.2013.doc assured that, he would mutate the 7/12 extracts.
In January, 2012 Subodh Parab told Respondent No.2 that, he would get the land partitioned in four shares and get four separate 7/12 extracts thereof.

Then, Mr. Subodh Parab, Mr. Mankar and Mr.
Machchhi
showed to Respondent No.2 a form for sub- division of the land and took him to Tahsil Office at Talasri.
There, they obtained Respondent No.2's signature on one paper having his photo and he was taken out of the Office.
On inquiry, they said that, the signature was taken for sub-division of the land.
4.1) On 05th June, 2012 Respondent No.2 went to the said bungalow along with friend Prakash Raut.
At that time, Petitioner No.1 along with one person came there and forcibly driven out Respondent No.2 from there.
Then, Petitioner No.1 took the Respondent No.2 at his residence and by showing him some documents, claimed that, he is owner of the said land.
Thereafter, Respondent No.2 contacted his acquaintance Mr. Sham Anna.
The later gave him a copy of the relevant papers of that property as were available with him.
Meanwhile, Respondent No.2 inquired with the Office of Tahasildar, Talasri.

It revealed that, the above said property has been sold to the Petitioners on the basis of a false irrevocable Power Of Attorney prepared in the name of Subodh Parab on the basis of a false P.O.A. prepared in the name of Respondent No.2 by forging his three brothers' signature.

2 further inquiry, Respondent No.2 learnt that, on 06 th March, 2012 Rs.5,50,000/- were credited in his bank account with Bank of P.H. Jayani 214 WP1499.2013.doc Baroda, Tardeo Branch, Mumbai by Bank of Baroda, Bordi Branch, Taluka Dahanu.

sentences.text: When Respondent No.2 visited the Bank of Baroda, Bordi Branch and checked, he found that, the pay-in-slip for said cheque payment was in the handwriting of Subodh Parab.

4.2) Thus, Subodh Parab obtained photo of Respondent No.2 and his brothers on a pretext of getting his land divided in the name of the four brothers and then between April 2011 and February 2012, Subodh Parab, Mr. Mankar, Petitioners and others made a false representation that they would get the said land partitioned in the name of the four brothers and thus deceiving Respondent No.2 obtained his signatures on blank papers in the office of Mr. Machchhi, Advocate.

Thereafter,
they prepared a false Power of Attorney in the name of Respondent No.2 using those photos and forging signature of his brothers and based on that prepared another false Power of Attorney in the name of Subodh Parab and using both the Power of Attorneys as genuine, executed the sale deed of the said property in the name of Petitioners.
However, except the last page, the signatures of Respondent No.2 on rest of the pages of the sale deed are forged.
Lastly, the said property got mutated in the name Petitioners, however, no prior notice of mutation was served upon Respondent No.2 and his brothers.
It is alleged that, Subodh Parab knew the said bank account of Respondent No.2.

On enquiry with Subodh Parab he revealed that, he had taken two cheques for Rs.3,00,000/-
which he deposited in his won account.
Hence, P.H. Jayani 214 WP1499.2013.doc Police registered this crime.
5) Learned Advocate for the Petitioners submitted that, initially a Power of Attorney dated 13th April, 2011 was executed by the three brothers in favour of Respondent No.2.
By virtue of this Power of Attorney, rights to sale the subject property, etc. were given to Respondent No.2 including to execute further Power of Attorney in favour of third person.
Accordingly, on 26th August, 2011 Respondent No.2 executed the 2nd Power of Attorney in favour of Subodh Parab which was registered at Sr.No.4245 in the office of Sub-Registrar, Talasri.
Then Respondent No.2 executed a declaration with the Office of the Sub-Registrar that, the first Power of Attorney is subsisting and binding upon all the vendors (brothers).
5.1) Learned Advocate submitted that, the Petitioners met with Respondent No.2 and Mr. Subodh Parab as they were desirous of purchasing the subject property.
Accordingly, the Petitioners purchased the property under the registered conveyance dated 27 th January, 2012 for a consideration of Rs.22,00,000/-.
Respondent No.2 himself was present in the Office of Sub-Registrar, Talasri and executed the deed of conveyance.
Both the Power of Attorneys were enclosed with this Deed of Conveyance.
In the backdrop, the Petitioners took possession of the said property and got it mutated in their name in the revenue record.
However, on 15 th July 2012, Respondent No.2 published a public notice that, the said Deed of Conveyance is obtained fraudulently.
The Public Notice was duly replied by P.H. Jayani 214 WP1499.2013.doc the Petitioners.
Later on, Respondent No.2 filed a civil suit bearing RCS No.82/2014 in Dahanu Court.
However, only for permanent injunction and not for cancellation of the Deed of Conveyance, etc.
Till date, the Respondent No.2 has not refunded the sale consideration of Rs.5,50,000/- credited in his bank account.
Thus, the impugned FIR is nothing but false as it is based on a concocted story.

sentences.text: To support the above submissions, learned Advocate relies upon the decision in Mohammed Ibrahim and Others Vs. State of Bihar and Another (2009) 8 Supreme Court Cases 751 wherein it is observed that, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has time and again drawn attention to the growing tendency of the complainants attempting to give the cloak of a criminal offence to matters which are essentially and purely civil in nature, obviously either to apply pressure on the accused, or out of enmity towards the accused, or to subject the accused to harassment.

entities.text: Mohammed Ibrahim and Others Vs. State of Bihar and Another (2009) 8 Supreme Court Cases 751
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Criminal courts should ensure that proceedings before it are not used for settling scores or to pressurise parties to settle civil disputes.

But at the same time, it should be noted that several disputes of a civil nature may also contain the ingredients of criminal offences and if so, will have to be tried as criminal offences, even if they also amount to civil disputes.

6) Per contra, learned APP submitted that, the impugned FIR clearly states that, the Petitioners and their co-accused prepared a false Power of Attorneys by misusing the photos of the four brothers and forging P.H. Jayani 214 WP1499.2013.doc signatures of the three brothers of Respondent No.2.
Then the accused using the Power of Attorneys as genuine, got the sale deed executed in favour of the Petitioners but forging his signatures thereon.
As such, there is prima facie case against the Petitioners of having committed the offence alleged in the impugned FIR.
7) Admittedly, the 1st Power of Attorney allegedly executed in favour of Respondent No.2 by his three brothers was prepared and registered on 13th April, 2011.

By virtue of this Power of Attorney,
right to sale the said property by accepting the consideration and other ancillary rights were given to Respondent No.2 by his brothers.
8) Admittedly, the Deed of Conveyance was executed by Respondent No.2 by going to the Office of Sub-Registrar, Talasri.
Considering the contents of this 1st Power of Attorney it is evident that, it was self sufficient to execute the subject Deed of Conveyance by Respondent No.2 on his and on his brothers' behalf.
Therefore, there was no need to execute the subsequent Power of Attorney in the name of Subodh Parab.
However, Subodh Parab caused the Respondent No.2 to execute the 2nd Power of Attorney in his favour based on the 1 st Power of Attorney.
Respondent No.2 has categorically alleged that, signatures of his brothers on the 1st Power of Attorney were forged.
Except the last page of the 2 nd Power of Attorney, the rest pages thereof does not bear signature of Respondent No.2.
Similarly, except the last page of the Deed of P.H. Jayani 214 WP1499.2013.doc Conveyance, the rest pages thereof does not bear full signature of Respondent No.2.
Moreover, his alleged initials on 1 st five pages of the alleged Deed of Conveyance does not tally with his initials on page nos.1 to 6 of the 1st Power of Attorney.
In view of the 1st Power of Attorney, there was no need of signature Subodh Parab on the Deed of Conveyance, however, he signed on it.
Moreover, the online registration details having photos of the parties are not enclosed with the subject Deed of Conveyance.
9) The FIR clearly mentions that, the pay-in-slip used to deposit the part sale consideration of Rs.5,50,000/- in the account Respondent No.2 was in the handwriting Subodh Parab.
Said amount was credited after 5 weeks of the registration of Deed of Conveyance, which is not normal.

The Petitioners have not explained as to when the cheques for balance consideration were deposited and credited in the bank account of the brothers of Respondent No.2.

As a result, the Petition is liable to be dismissed and is accordingly dismissed.
